why:
phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode(node_name[, namespace], options = NodeOptions())`, upstream's constructor, plus `(NodeHandle, name[, namespace])` for the component model. Construction cannot throw (RFC-0018), so a failure leaves `ok()` false, as `rclcpp::Node`'s does — the envelope. Upstream's trailing `bool enable_communication_interface` is not taken.

Before phase-482 W4: theirs `(name[, namespace], NodeOptions&, bool)`, ours `()` / `(void* executor_handle)` (plus a deleted copy ctor). Every position is accounted for by a rule or a constraint: `NodeOptions&` is `compile-time-options`; `make_shared`-style construction is `no-shared-ptr` (see `cpp:LifecycleNode::make_shared`); the name and namespace are not construction parameters because the node is created by the executor from baked boot config (RFC-0045), not named at the call site; and the trailing `bool enable_communication_interface` is our explicit `register_services()` / `autostart()` -- `rclc_executor_register_lifecycle_services` registers all five REP-2002 servers (`~/change_state`, `~/get_state`, `~/get_available_states`, `~/get_available_transitions`, `~/get_transition_graph`) in ONE call, explicitly, because each server is a zenoh queryable against `ZPICO_MAX_QUERYABLES` (issue 0460) -- see the service stage's `c:executor_register_lifecycle_services`. The `void*` handle rather than an `Executor&` is the house idiom (`Executor::handle()` returns `void*`), not a lifecycle decision. our `nros::LifecycleNode` is a MIXIN over an executor handle, not a `Node` subclass: RFC-0002 puts one executor per RTOS task and the lifecycle state machine lives on the EXECUTOR (that is what `rclc_executor_lifecycle_*` and `register_lifecycle_services` drive), while the node-side API stays on `nros::Node`. rclcpp's `LifecycleNode` re-declares the whole `Node` surface because it cannot inherit from `Node`; ours does not need to, and duplicating ~50 methods onto a second class would cost image size for nothing. What a ported node loses: it holds a `Node&` and a `LifecycleNode` instead of one object.
